title: The most frequent words first
body: About 3,000 word families cover roughly 90% of everyday conversation. Learning in frequency order means every word you learn pays off immediately.
source: Nation (2006); Davies, A Frequency Dictionary of Spanish

title: Spaced repetition
body: Reviewing a word just as you're about to forget it makes the memory last longer. The review queue schedules every card for you.

title: Chunks, not just words
body: Native speakers lean on ready-made phrases (¿me da…?, ¿qué onda?). Learning them whole gets you speaking faster and helps you hear them in fast speech.
